existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicinalProductManufactured` has material breaking changes: the R4 resource is absent in R6 and is apparently replaced by `ManufacturedItemDefinition`. The top migration concerns are resource identity, mandatory R6 `status`, and non-mechanical remapping of `quantity`, ingredients, and physical characteristics. The main uncertainty is the absence of an official ConceptMap or narrative migration note.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a model transformation rather than a resource rename. Existing R4 data must change resource type and canonical references, assign an R6 lifecycle `status`, decide how to preserve the mandatory R4 `quantity`, translate ingredient references into R6 `Ingredient`/coded ingredient patterns, and remodel physical characteristics into R6 `property` entries. R6-to-R4 conversion is also lossy because R6 can carry identifiers, marketing status, components, and coded properties that the R4 resource did not support.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the assigned R6 resource name is absent and that `ManufacturedItemDefinition` is the likely successor, based on the R6 package index, `fhir-old-types`, `fhir-types`, and matching retained elements. Confidence is medium for precise migration recommendations because the local inputs do not include an official diff, ConceptMap, narrative migration page, or terminology expansions for the example bindings.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
MedicinalProductManufactured has a resource-identity break: R4 MedicinalProductManufactured resource is absent in R6 and appears renamed/replaced by ManufacturedItemDefinition. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 95/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

2 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.

topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen; old-valid/new-invalid also applies because an R4 `resourceType: MedicinalProductManufactured` instance is not an R6 resource, and generated models/routes keyed by the old name fail without a transform.

topFindings.title: Mandatory R4 quantity has no direct R6 successor element
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid; retaining `quantity` under the R6 successor creates an unknown element, while dropping it creates possible R6-to-R4 loss because R4 cannot be reconstructed without inventing a mandatory value.

topFindings.title: R6 successor adds mandatory modifier status with a required publication-status binding
